## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṅgahitavāra* ("The classes of offenses to which each rule belongs") is a section within the *Parivāra*, the concluding book of the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka. In keeping with the mnemonic and analytical nature of the *Parivāra*, the text systematically defines which monastic rules and offense classes fall under or are comprised within the heading of other rules. It has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

No cross-language parallels are recorded for the *Saṅgahitavāra* in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit corpora [DharmaNexus]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus documents extensive intra-Pali textual reuse, detecting 139 matching passages across 21 other texts, all located within the *Parivāra* [DharmaNexus]. Its strongest textual connections are with the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4; 33 matches, longest §1.2–1.3 ↔ §80.5–80.6), the *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11; 20 matches, longest §1.2–1.3 ↔ §31.4–31.5), and the *Samuccayavāra* (Pvr 1.8; 13 matches) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits direct structural and verbal duplication with corresponding vāra sections, including the homonymous *Saṅgahitavāra* of the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga analysis (Pvr 1.12; §0.3–3.1 ↔ §0.3–3.1) and the *Saṅgahavāra* texts (Pvr 2.4 and Pvr 2.12) [DharmaNexus]. None of the surveyed secondary literature directly examines this specific Vinaya text.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
